refuted.claim_tested: first yen within 7-21 days from a maintained, normalised, diffable public-data feed sold by subscription
refuted.finding: The complaint is real and sourced — LiteLLM's price table is measurably incomplete (15 models missing, GitHub issue #22646, 2026-03-03), custom model prices do not reach cost calculation so spend reads $0.00 (#11975, 2025-06-23, re-reported 2026-03-11 and 2026-05-19), and per-provider dimensions such as cache read/write break a plain input/output table (#27191). But the space is occupied by a free incumbent, and not a thin one: Portkey Models is a free, auth-free API covering 2,000+ models across 40+ providers with normalised pricing including cache, image, video and search dimensions, used by 200+ companies for cost calculation on 400B tokens/day. It already solves most of the complaint the estimate rested on. No case was found of a normalised LLM-pricing feed converting free users to paid at all. The nearest first-yen example in an adjacent data API is Canopy API at about 12 days (public 2023-01-24, first organic paying customer 2023-02-05) — and that launch was an Indie Hackers post recruiting users with a discount offer, with any pre-existing readership unverified.
refuted.verdict: does not meet the 7-21 day claim as stated
refuted.not_refuted: that maintained data feeds can be sold. Only this candidate's speed from a standing start with no audience — and note nobody has yet shown paid demand for this particular feed at all, which is weaker than the other two, where monetisation was confirmed.

refuted.claim_tested: many individually findable pages, each carrying something computed rather than templated, reach a first buyer from zero audience with no recurring human posting, because a third party can discover and refer one
refuted.finding: No case was found with the full causal chain and both calendar dates. The nearest fast case (PredictionJobs, first $100 within 10 days) is the one this candidate was modelled on, and its own author attributes the sale to a large X account's post, not to search: there is no evidence the referrer found a specific page through search, and the pages were combinatorial templates rather than computed. Three counter-examples hit the candidate directly. Causal mass-published ~1,800 low-originality pages and took a Google manual action: organic traffic -99.52% (307,158 -> 1,485) over 2023-08 to 2024-08. Datanyze is the closest counter-example, because it had exactly what this candidate proposes — genuine per-entity data on each page — and still lost 95.46% of organic traffic, with over 80% of the loss concentrated in the two programmatic directories; the pages stayed HTTP 200 and indexed and were re-ranked down anyway. Stripe Fee Auditor tested the computed-value premise on its own: three months, 4,230 search impressions, 5 clicks, 2 real users, ¥0 — and Hacker News sent more real users in three hours than three months of search did. Google's own position matches: scaled content abuse (2024-03-05) covers mass low-originality pages whether generated or hand-written, and Search Essentials states outright that meeting the requirements does not guarantee crawl, index or display, and lists telling relevant communities as a basic step.
refuted.verdict: falls as a route to first yen from zero audience without recurring posting
refuted.not_refuted: that many search surfaces can work as a long-term acquisition play, and that per-page substance matters. What was refuted is this candidate's role: a route that reaches a FIRST buyer unattended. Note the survey answered the sub-question too — no case supports 'one computed value per page is enough'. The near-successes carried a page that could be acted on by itself (BuiltWith's technology list, IPinfo's IP metadata, Tunebat's key/BPM), and even those cannot be attributed to search for the first sale.
refuted.what_it_leaves: Four candidates have now been refuted by outside evidence and every one of them failed on the same term. In each near-success the first buyer arrived through a third party with reach posting about the thing — an X account, Hacker News, Product Hunt, Stack Overflow answers — and never through discovery working unattended. distribution_answer already elected route 2 (findable surfaces) over route 1 (post where the buyers already gather) not on evidence but on our own constraint that recurring owner actions are excluded; it said so plainly. This survey removes the evidence route 2 was resting on, so what remains is a constraint with no surviving route under it. That is a decision for a lap to take deliberately, not a gap to fill by proposing a sixth build candidate.

Monetisation is real and confirmed with sources (Order Limit Pro USD 49/yr; Independent Analytics Pro USD 49-199/yr, licence keys). What could not be found is any case of first yen reached on new directory traffic alone: the one same-day sale on record (Independent Analytics) launched to an existing user base and an announcement post, and the counter-example (Gato GraphQL) took about 2.5 months.
refuted.verdict: does not meet the 7-21 day claim as stated
refuted.not_refuted: that WordPress plugins can be sold, or that this complaint exists. Only this candidate's speed from a standing start with no list.
